title: Algorithms to Live By

Allbery reports that chapters explain algorithms, compare human decisions and examine empirical studies; their explanatory value survives even where practical advice adds little. Philosophical implications and daily-life advice support the explanatory argument rather than make it a philosophical treatise. T11=T12=0. It is not about a bounded historical period, so H13=0. title: Startup
author: Jerry Kaplan

title: The Gray Lady Winked
author: Ashley Rindsberg
reason: A polemical historical account of newspaper failures, not a manual. The publisher’s claims about world-historical causation are much stronger than the demonstrated evidence reviewed here. rationale: E/A: selected episodes and expansive causal claims require a low assessment. S/U/M/F: ownership and agenda-setting offer modest mechanisms, with limited comparative control. D/R: case repetition and controversy dependence reduce value. N/P: readable but rhetorically sweeping.

title: The Long Tail
author: Chris Anderson
reason: A sustained economic explanation of digital distribution, not a marketing procedure manual. The central prediction about niche demand faces empirical challenge; retain the cost-and-search mechanism while lowering evidence and certainty. Media markets dominate the examples and thesis (T12).
rationale: E/A: useful market data with contested aggregation and forecasts. S/U/M/F: search and distribution costs provide reusable mechanisms, not a universal shift away from hits. D/R: repeated cases and dated expectations limit lasting value. N/P: clear thesis, overstated scope.

title: Who Really Matters
author: Art Kleiner

rationale: E/A: cases and consulting access, weak independent causal tests. S/U/M/F: expectations, influence and resource allocation give reusable organizational mechanisms. D/R: one core thesis is repeated, but informal authority persists. N/P: readable conceptual framing.

title: Am I Being Too Subtle?
author: Sam Zell
reason: An investor memoir with advice embedded in deals and personal history, rather than a valuation manual. Supply-demand mismatches and asset cycles provide transferable content. Finance is central.
rationale: E/A: direct experience with strong survivor bias. S/U/M/F: asset scarcity, leverage and timing offer moderate strategic utility. D/R: memoir overhead; basic cyclical constraints endure. N/P: clear, assertive, sometimes self-serving.

title: Amazon Unbound
author: Brad Stone
reason: Reported account of Amazon’s expansion, not a company-operating guide. Computing, logistics, platform incentives and industrial scale are central; media and political power are important applications. International scope avoids T11.
rationale: E/A: substantial reporting, with access limits. S/U/M/F: cloud services, fulfillment, markets and governance connect strongly. D/R: founder and personal episodes lower density; scaling constraints endure. N/P: clear, well-organized reporting.

title: Andrew Carnegie
author: David Nasaw
reason: A researched industrial biography with enough production, finance and institutional mechanisms to pass V3. Its broad personal and philanthropic scope makes US historical development predominant (T11), while steel and enterprise remain central rather than politics alone.

title: Black Box Thinking
author: Matthew Syed

rationale: E/A: reported cases and psychology, with limited causal control. S/U/M/F: reporting incentives, feedback and blame connect organizations to reliability. D/R: recurring examples reduce density; learning constraints are durable. N/P: clear, occasionally too binary.

title: Blink
author: Malcolm Gladwell
reason: A popular explanatory account of rapid judgment, not a decision workbook. No serious central factual failure was established by the evidence reviewed. Correct original publication to 2005.
rationale: E/A: selective studies and narrative cases constrain inferential integrity. S/U/M/F: recognition and bias explain some decisions, with weak boundary conditions. D/R: extended anecdotes and fragile research claims reduce density and durability. N/P: excellent storytelling, compressed ambiguity.

author: Bernie Marcus; Arthur Blank; Bob Andelman

rationale: E/A: participant access with self-presentation bias. S/U/M/F: retail layout, purchasing and service link operations and incentives. D/R: personal stories reduce density; business constraints endure. N/P: clear, direct narrative.

author: Sheila Bair

author: Ted Turner; Bill Burke

rationale: E/A: access and recollection with strong self-presentation limits. S/U/M/F: distribution economics and corporate combinations offer modest transfer. D/R: sports and personal episodes reduce density; some industry lessons endure. N/P: lively but selective.

author: Kurt Eichenwald

rationale: E/A: extensive reporting, reconstruction limits. S/U/M/F: accounting, incentives, opaque contracts and governance connect strongly. D/R: a large cast and length lower density; fraud mechanisms endure. N/P: coherent narrative and controlled prose.

title: Dear Chairman
author: Jeff Gramm
reason: A history of shareholder activism built around original letters, not an investing manual or civil-activism tract. Corporate governance supplies transferable mechanisms. The largely US financial history triggers both thematic deductions. Correct the catalog’s 2015 date to the 2016 book.
rationale: E/A: primary letters and financial expertise, with selected campaign cases. S/U/M/F: ownership, managers and incentives connect. D/R: focused source-centered chapters, durable governance conflicts. N/P: clear and precise.

title: Delivering Happiness
author: Tony Hsieh
reason: A business autobiography that explains the development of Zappos and its culture. The main sequence is narrative; advice is embedded rather than a standalone operating manual. Service, incentives and capital constraints provide reusable content.
rationale: E/A: founder testimony with survivor and self-attribution limits. S/U/M/F: service economics, staffing and customer retention give a modest model. D/R: motivational sections reduce density and durability. N/P: clear, informal storytelling.

title: Different
author: Youngme Moon
reason: An essayistic critique of competitive imitation and product sameness, not a step-by-step marketing system. Differentiation and convergence provide a transferable model; selected examples constrain proof.
rationale: E/A: marketing scholarship and cases, weak causal identification. S/U/M/F: competitive imitation, features and consumer attention connect moderately. D/R: repeated theme limits density, enduring strategic question. N/P: readable and conceptually clear.

title: Dream Big
author: Cristiane Correa
reason: A reported history of Lemann, Telles and Sicupira and their global business expansion. It is not a business-method manual. Acquisitions and capital allocation are central (T12); the reach is international. Use the 2013 Portuguese original.

title: Hard Landing
author: Thomas Petzinger
reason: Reported history of airline competition and deregulation, not an airline-management manual. Capacity, networks, pricing and labor provide strong mechanisms. US airline restructuring is the central historical object, despite international consequences (T11).
rationale: E/A: sustained industry reporting with elite-access limits. S/U/M/F: regulation, aircraft economics, route networks and incentives connect strongly. D/R: large cast lowers density; capacity and coordination problems endure. N/P: clear, controlled narrative.

title: Hate Inc.
author: Matt Taibbi
reason: A reported and confessional critique of media incentives. It is an explanatory polemic rather than an operational guide or a program for a political movement. Audience sorting and monetized outrage provide a payload; sweeping equivalences reduce evidence. US media politics triggers both thematic deductions.
rationale: E/A: practitioner access, selective examples and strong rhetoric. S/U/M/F: attention, advertising and partisan audience incentives connect usefully. D/R: repetition and immediate controversies reduce durability. N/P: forceful prose, weak qualification.

title: Hit Refresh
author: Satya Nadella; Greg Shaw; Jill Tracie Nichols
reason: A memoir and account of Microsoft’s organizational change, with future technology discussion secondary. It passes the hard gates and high-tech memoir exception. The corporate narrative is promotional but not shown to depend centrally on a serious error.
rationale: E/A: direct executive access, limited external challenge. S/U/M/F: culture, cloud platforms and strategic change supply moderate mechanisms. D/R: inspirational repetition and forecasts lower lasting value. N/P: readable, sometimes promotional.

title: Iacocca
author: Lee Iacocca; William Novak

title: Innovating Out of Crisis
author: Shigetaka Komori
reason: A CEO’s explanatory account of Fujifilm’s diversification after film demand collapsed. The core is a corporate transformation narrative rather than technical training. rationale: E/A: direct technical-business access with self-attribution limits. S/U/M/F: chemistry, products, capital and demand shifts connect strongly. D/R: concise case and durable capability-reuse lessons. N/P: clear, somewhat promotional.

title: Limping on Water
author: Phil Beuth
reason: A television-executive memoir and corporate history, not a production manual. Acquisition discipline and organizational trust provide a modest payload. US broadcasting dominates both themes. The central forty-year Capital Cities career ends around the Disney acquisition in 1996.
rationale: E/A: participant testimony with memory and loyalty limits. S/U/M/F: broadcasting, acquisitions and management relationships connect modestly. D/R: extensive personal material lowers density; some governance lessons endure. N/P: readable reminiscence.

title: Master Of The Game
author: Connie Bruck
reason: Reported biography of Steve Ross and the formation of Time Warner. Deal structure, ownership and incentives provide enough payload to avoid V3. US media and a media mogul dominate both themes; Ross’s career ends in 1992.
rationale: E/A: investigative access and reporting, with motive-reconstruction limits. S/U/M/F: media assets, finance and organizational power connect moderately. D/R: personal detail lowers density; acquisition incentives remain useful. N/P: strong narrative and controlled prose.

title: Merchants of Truth
author: Jill Abramson
reason: A reported comparison of four news organizations, not a journalism manual. rationale: E/A: broad access offset by acknowledged sourcing problems and uneven fact checking. S/U/M/F: advertising, platforms and newsroom incentives provide modest mechanisms. D/R: lengthy personalities and recent disputes lower durability. N/P: readable, weakened factual control.

title: My Forty Years with Ford
author: Charles E. Sorensen; Samuel T. Williamson

rationale: E/A: direct production experience with retrospective and personal-conflict limits. S/U/M/F: tooling, flow, labor and factory coordination connect strongly. D/R: concentrated operational detail, durable production constraints. N/P: clear, concrete narrative.

title: My Years with General Motors
author: Alfred Sloan
reason: A sustained historical and explanatory account of GM’s organization. Production and large-scale organization are central.
rationale: E/A: direct records and executive access with institutional self-defense. S/U/M/F: divisions, financial control, products and scale form a strong integrated account. D/R: detailed but largely purposeful; coordination problems endure. N/P: controlled, sometimes dry exposition.

title: No Filter
author: Sarah Frier
reason: A reported history of Instagram and its relationship to Facebook. It passes the narrative gate and has platform incentives and acquisition-governance lessons. Social media is the central product and institution (T12); international influence avoids T11.
rationale: E/A: extensive interviews, access and motive limits. S/U/M/F: network growth, advertising, design and ownership connect. D/R: personality drama lowers density; platform lessons partly endure. N/P: clear and controlled.

title: Priceless
author: William Poundstone
reason: A popular explanation of price perception and behavioral experiments, not a pricing-method manual. Anchoring, context and incentives provide reusable mechanisms; marketing applications do not make finance the central topic.
rationale: E/A: experimental synthesis with replication and generalization limits. S/U/M/F: perception, value and market framing connect moderately. D/R: anecdotes repeat, but contextual valuation remains relevant. N/P: clear, sometimes stronger than the evidence.

title: Representing Talent
author: Violaine Roussel
reason: An explanatory ethnography of talent agents and valuation, not a technical reference or agent-training manual. The publisher presents it for readers seeking to understand the industry. US Hollywood media and power dominate both themes; the analysis is not centered on one historical period.
rationale: E/A: fieldwork and explicit research limitations support integrity. S/U/M/F: relationships, reputation and brokerage explain value formation with cross-industry transfer. D/R: narrow detail lowers density; brokerage mechanisms endure. N/P: careful but academic prose.

title: Roger Ailes
author: Zev Chafets

rationale: E/A: unusually close access, weak distance from the subject. S/U/M/F: media distribution and political influence supply limited explanation. D/R: personality emphasis and pre-scandal perspective reduce durability. N/P: readable, selective framing.

title: Saving Capitalism from Short Termism
author: Alfred Rappaport
reason: A sustained argument about short-term incentives and shareholder value. Specific reform proposals support the explanation rather than a stepwise training method. Financial governance is central; recommendations alone do not establish ideological capture or political activism.
rationale: E/A: established financial analysis, with causal simplification of crisis mechanisms. S/U/M/F: compensation, investor horizons and governance connect. D/R: focused thesis and durable incentive problems. N/P: clear, sometimes prescriptive certainty.

title: Setting The Table
author: Danny Meyer
reason: A mixed restaurant memoir and hospitality argument. The central account is the history and philosophy of actual restaurants, not recipes or a procedural operating guide. Staffing priorities and service feedback offer a payload. New York restaurant development dominates T11.
rationale: E/A: direct experience with survivor bias. S/U/M/F: service, staff incentives and customer relationships connect moderately. D/R: biographical overhead, durable coordination lessons. N/P: engaging and concrete.

title: Slugfest
author: Reed Tucker
reason: A nonfiction history of Marvel–DC competition, not fiction or comic-drawing instruction. Distribution, intellectual-property control and creative incentives provide a payload. US media industry history triggers both deductions.
rationale: E/A: reported interviews and history, selective participant memory. S/U/M/F: rights, distribution and talent markets connect modestly. D/R: fan and personality detail reduces density; industry incentives endure. N/P: lively and clear.

title: Small Is the New Big
author: Seth Godin
reason: An essay and blog-post collection rather than a systematic how-to reference. General observations on scale, marketing and organizational choice provide some transferable content, although the account is fragmented and weakly evidenced. Low fit is not an exclusion.
rationale: E/A: anecdotal assertions with little systematic validation. S/U/M/F: small-scale coordination and differentiation offer modest heuristics. D/R: repetition and dated posts reduce density and durability. N/P: punchy but conceptually loose.

title: That Will Never Work
author: Marc Randolph
reason: A founder’s narrative of Netflix’s early formation, not a company-building manual. Product-market experiments, logistics and subscription incentives supply a durable payload. The central account ends with Randolph’s departure in 2003; later Netflix scale is context.
rationale: E/A: participant detail with retrospective self-attribution limits. S/U/M/F: distribution, experiments and business models connect. D/R: personal episodes cost density; early-stage constraints endure. N/P: coherent and readable.

title: The Basic Laws of Human Stupidity
author: Carlo Cipolla

author: Michael S. Malone

title: The Billionaire Shell Game
author: L. J. Davis

rationale: E/A: reported deals and interviews with motive limits. S/U/M/F: networks, debt and managerial incentives connect moderately. D/R: personalities and dated forecasts lower density and durability. N/P: clear, sometimes theatrical.

author: Ian Goldin; Mike Mariathasan

author: Jonathan A. Knee; Bruce C. Greenwald; Ava Seave

title: The Death of the Artist
author: William Deresiewicz

author: Joe Ricketts

author: Michael Lewis

author: Eric Jackson

author: Clayton M. Christensen

author: Brent Schlender; Rick Tetzeli

title: AI Superpowers
author: Kai-Fu Lee

rationale: Practical authority supports A; forecasts and national comparisons limit E. S/U/M/F retain commercialization mechanisms. Personal passages reduce D. Rapidly changing examples lower R; N is clear and P sometimes overconfident.

title: New Power

rationale: E/M/P are limited by selected examples and a coarse taxonomy. Network participation supports S/U/F. Repetition lowers D; topical cases lower R. Authors’ organizing experience supports A; N is accessible.

title: Super Pumped

reason: A popular narrative survey of selected philosophers and their ideas, not a technical textbook or specialist reference. It spans antiquity to the author’s present without a single central historical period. Selection and simplification lower evidence but the conceptual payload prevents V3.
rationale: E/A: broad learned synthesis, dated interpretations and selective canon. S/U/M/F: intellectual and social contexts connect moderately, limited operational mechanisms. D/R: biography and digressions lower density, philosophical questions endure. N/P: readable narrative, sometimes overconfident compression.

title: The Wisdom of Life
author: Arthur Schopenhauer
reason: A philosophical essay on happiness, temperament, possessions and reputation, extracted from Parerga and Paralipomena. Advice is embedded in sustained argument rather than a technical procedure or training course. Its pessimistic psychology is conjectural. Use the original 1851 work, not the 1888 translation.
rationale: E/A: philosophical importance with unsupported generalizations and period prejudice. S/U/M/F: modest heuristics on desire and reputation, little causal or systems depth. D/R: compact thematic argument and durable concerns. N/P: clear structure, sharp but sweeping judgments.

title: When Reason Goes on Holiday
author: Neven Sesardic
reason: A critical historical argument about philosophers’ political judgments. Its selected examples and polemical framing lower evidence, but criticism of political allegiance is not itself proof of ideological capture. It supplies a lesson about expertise outside domain; no sufficiently demonstrated serious V1 or V2 is inferred from disagreement alone.
rationale: E/A: documented intellectual cases with asymmetric selection and limited comparison groups. S/U/M/F: status, expertise and ideological incentives connect moderately; weak causal identification. D/R: focused but repetitive case pattern, lasting warning beyond current disputes. N/P: clear polemic, sometimes broad conclusions.

title: Destined For War
author: Graham Allison
reason: A comparative argument about rising and established powers. The author’s project openly lists sixteen selected cases; these do not define an unbiased sample from which a war probability can be read. The book explicitly allows avoiding war, so its title is not evidence of fatalistic prediction. No serious veto is established.
rationale: E/M/P are limited by case selection and analogy. S/U/F retain security and institutional constraints. D/N are focused, R moderate and A policy-research authority.

title: The Rise And Fall Of American Growth
author: Robert J. Gordon
reason: A sustained economic history of living standards and technological change, not an economics textbook. Measurement, complementary infrastructure and diffusion provide strong payload. The forecast of slower growth is more uncertain than the historical reconstruction. American scope triggers T11; finance is not the central topic.
rationale: E/A credit extensive economic measurement with forecast limits. S/U/M/F integrate technology, households and production. Length reduces D, R is strong for history but lower for projections, N/P clear.

title: Titan
author: Ron Chernow
reason: A biography of Rockefeller integrating oil production, transport, pricing and organization. Industrial scaling provides payload; it is not an investing manual. The substantial American personal and institutional focus triggers T11, while the central subject is industrial business rather than finance alone.
rationale: E/A credit historical research. S/U/M/F connect integration and market power. Length lowers D; R/N/P retain durable controlled narrative.

title: The Last Lion: Defender of the Realm, 1940–1965
author: William Manchester; Paul Reid
reason: The product is The Last Lion: Defender of the Realm, 1940–1965, the final Churchill volume by Manchester and Reid. It is political-military biography with coalition and strategic constraints, not a doctrine manual.
rationale: E/A credit researched biography. S/U/M/F concern alliances and command. Very large personal narrative lowers D; R/N/P remain strong.

title: Faraday, Maxwell, and the Electromagnetic Field
author: Nancy Forbes; Basil Mahon
reason: A scientific dual biography and account of the field concept. Experiment, mathematics and intellectual communication provide payload; it is not electromagnetism training. Familiar physics limits incremental utility for this reader.
rationale: E/A credit researched scientific exposition. S/U/M/F connect experimental and mathematical work. D/R/N/P credit focused durable explanation.

title: From Bacteria to Bach and Back
author: Daniel C. Dennett
reason: A sustained philosophical and scientific argument about competence, cultural evolution and consciousness. It is not a neuroscience textbook. Mechanistic proposals are substantial, but analogies and contested interpretations reduce confidence.
rationale: E/M/P reflect disputed explanatory reach. S/U/F connect cognition, computation and culture. D reduced by long argument, R/A strong, N clear.

title: Guns, Sails, and Empires
author: Carlo M. Cipolla
reason: An explanatory technological history of guns, ships, commerce and European expansion. It is neither a gunnery manual nor a specialist engineering reference. Military use is an application of the central technology account, so T12=0.
rationale: E/A credit economic-historical synthesis with age limits. S/U/M/F strongly integrate technical constraints and trade. D/R/N/P credit compact durable explanation.

title: Medieval Technology and Social Change
author: Lynn White Jr.
reason: Three sustained historical arguments about technology, agriculture and mechanical power, not an instructional textbook despite classroom use. The stirrup-to-feudalism argument is seriously contested and is not treated as established fact. Broader material-culture mechanisms remain useful; inspected scholarly evidence does not establish a fatal dependency of all three arguments.
rationale: E/M/P are reduced for causal overreach. S/U/F retain technology-society connections, A recognizes serious specialist attention rather than correctness. D/R are strong and N moderately clear.

title: The Ancient City
author: Peter Connolly; Hazel Dodge
reason: An illustrated explanatory reconstruction of Athens and Rome for general readers. Its coherent account of buildings and urban life passes rule 2; it is not a construction reference. Infrastructure and civic organization provide payload. The comparative cross-period treatment has no single central endpoint.
rationale: E/A credit archaeological reconstruction with uncertainty. S/U/M/F concern urban infrastructure and social use. D/R/N/P credit visual explanation and durable scope.

title: The Great Crash, 1929
author: John Kenneth Galbraith
reason: An explanatory financial history of speculation, leverage and collapse. It is not investment instruction. Use the 1955 original rather than the later edition’s 2009 library date.
rationale: E/A credit economic analysis with retrospective limits. S/U/M/F concern credit, incentives and financial fragility. D/R/N/P credit compact durable clear narrative.

title: The Old Way
author: Elizabeth Marshall Thomas
reason: An ethnographic memoir about hunter-gatherer life. Cooperation, sharing and resource constraints provide modest mechanisms; it is not a survival manual. Retrospective generalization from one community limits confidence.
rationale: E/A credit direct observation with memory and representativeness limits. S/U/M concern social-resource arrangements; F low. D/R/N/P retain readable durable account.

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
reason: A sustained general scientific argument for evolution by natural selection, not a modern biology course or specialist procedure reference. Its historical explanatory value is assessed explicitly; obsolete inheritance details are not represented as current science.
rationale: E/A credit foundational evidence and argument with known historical limits. S/U/M/F retain selection and comparative reasoning. Long evidential accumulation lowers D/N; R/P remain strong.

title: The Red Queen
author: Matt Ridley
reason: A popular explanation of sexual selection and evolutionary psychology. It is not a biology textbook. Coevolution and strategic interaction provide payload; extrapolation to human behavior and aging examples constrain confidence.
rationale: E/M/P are lower for broad adaptive explanations. S/U/F retain evolutionary strategic ideas. D/N readable, R moderate and A skilled synthesis.

title: The Age of Napoleon
author: Will Durant; Ariel Durant
reason: Assess volume XI, The Age of Napoleon, separately from the other nominated Story of Civilization volumes. This is general narrative history, not a textbook. European institutions and resources provide payload, but the central political leader and wars trigger both themes. Its original year is 1975, not the first year of the whole series.
rationale: E/A reflect broad secondary synthesis and dated scholarship. S/U/M/F connect states, culture and resources. D low for length, R durable, N/P fluent but sweeping.

title: Rousseau and Revolution
author: Will Durant; Ariel Durant
reason: Assess volume X, Rousseau and Revolution, as its own nominated work. Intellectual change, institutions and the preconditions of revolution supply payload. This is a history of philosophical and political movements, not advocacy of their doctrines; V5 does not follow merely from its subjects. Central philosophy and revolution trigger T12.
rationale: E/A reflect wide secondary synthesis rather than current specialist consensus. S/U/M/F connect ideas and institutions. D low for immense scope, R/N/P retain durable readable history.

title: The Age of Louis XIV
author: Will Durant; Ariel Durant
reason: Assess volume VIII, The Age of Louis XIV. Despite its title, it is a European civilizational account spanning science, literature, art, religion and institutions, not chiefly a biography of Louis XIV. Scientific organization and cultural institutions provide some payload; the broad mix does not establish a predominant T11 or T12 topic.
rationale: E/A reflect dated general synthesis. S/U/M/F connect intellectual and institutional change. D low for extensive life detail; R/N/P credit durable narrative.

title: The Age of Reason Begins
author: Will Durant; Ariel Durant
reason: Assess volume VII, The Age of Reason Begins. The narrative connects scientific change, commerce, institutions and culture across Europe. It is not science training, and religious conflicts are historical subjects rather than devotional advocacy. Broad cultural and scientific development is the central account.
rationale: E/A reflect dated synthesis. S/U/M/F credit connections around inquiry and institutions. D moderate to low for long biographical passages; R/N/P retain durable readable history.

title: The Age of Voltaire
author: Will Durant; Ariel Durant
reason: Assess volume IX, The Age of Voltaire. The publisher specifies the conflict between religion and philosophy as a special center. This is historical interpretation rather than a religious or ideological manifesto. Intellectual networks and institutional authority supply payload; central philosophy triggers T12.
rationale: E/A reflect broad old synthesis. S/U/M/F concern ideas, institutions and cultural change. D low for biographical detail; R/N/P credit durable fluent narrative.

title: Tuxedo Park
author: Jennet Conant
reason: A scientific and institutional biography of Alfred Loomis’s laboratory and wartime research networks. Funding, coordination and translating research into radar provide payload. War is an application of the central science-organization story.
rationale: E/A credit historical research with person-centered framing limits. S/U/M/F strongly connect science, money and institutions. D/R/N/P credit focused durable narrative.

title: A History of Knowledge
author: Charles Van Doren
reason: A chronological narrative of ideas rather than a narrow technical reference, despite marketing as a one-volume reference. It passes rule 2. Broad connections offer payload, but compression and future speculation limit depth.
rationale: E/A are broad synthesis rather than specialist verification. S/U/M/F retain intellectual connections with low causal detail. D/R/N/P are moderate.

title: A History of Rome
author: Moses Hadas
reason: An edited narrative assembled from Roman historians, not a technical or instructional textbook. Institutions and power transitions give modest payload, but ancient sources and selection limit causal certainty.
rationale: E/A reflect source criticism limits and scholarly editing. S/U/M/F modest. D/R credit compact historical reach; N/P less cumulative because multiple original voices are combined.

title: A History of the English-Speaking Peoples
author: Winston S. Churchill
reason: A multi-volume narrative history of Britain and its related polities. Assess the nominated series using first-volume 1956 publication. Its national-cultural framing and selective politics reduce confidence; no serious ideological veto is established solely by Churchill’s identity.
rationale: E/M/P are limited by selective retrospective synthesis. S/U/F concern institutions and state power. Very broad narrative lowers D; R/A/N retain historical and literary strengths.

title: America's War for the Greater Middle East
author: Andrew J. Bacevich
reason: A critical narrative of US military policy across the greater Middle East. Strategic objectives, operational mismatch and institutional inertia provide payload. Criticism of policy is not alone proof of ideological capture or an activist manifesto.
rationale: E/A credit historical synthesis with argumentative selection limits. S/U/M/F concern strategy and institutions. D/R/N/P retain durable readable account.

title: American Nations
author: Colin Woodard
reason: A cross-period argument about persistent American regional cultures. Settlement and institutions offer hypotheses, but stable cultural categories can overstate continuity and understate within-region variation. No serious veto is established by the inspected evidence.
rationale: E/M/P are limited by broad typology. S/U/F concern institutions and geography. D/R moderate, A journalistic and N clear.

title: Black Elk
author: Joe Jackson
reason: A historical biography of a religious figure rather than a book advocating his religion. Cultural adaptation, authority and institutions provide modest payload. The Indigenous and American history focus triggers T11.
rationale: E/A credit researched biography. S/U/M/F remain modest institutional interpretation. D reduced by life detail; R/N/P retain durable narrative.

title: Bloodlands
author: Timothy Snyder
reason: A comparative history of mass killing under Nazi and Soviet regimes. State capacity, occupation and policy interaction provide institutional mechanisms. The comparative framework is debated, but that does not alone establish V1 or ideological capture.
rationale: E/A credit multilingual historical research with comparative-frame limits. S/U/M/F concern state violence. D moderate, R/N/P strong.

title: Bowling Alone
author: Robert D. Putnam
reason: A research-based explanatory account of changing association and social capital in America. It is neither a sociology textbook nor primarily an activist manual. Measurement and causal attribution remain less secure than the descriptive trends.
rationale: E/A credit empirical social research. S/U/M/F concern networks and institutions. Length reduces D; R/N/P retain durable clear synthesis.

title: Brute
author: Robert Coram
reason: A biography of Victor Krulak, not a tactical manual. Amphibious organization, adaptation and institutional politics give payload. Correct the source author’s misspelling from Koram to Coram.
rationale: E/A credit biography with admiring-frame limits. S/U/M/F concern technical-operational and organizational constraints. D/R/N/P remain moderate to strong.

title: City of the Century
author: Donald L. Miller
reason: A narrative history of Chicago linking transport, engineering, commerce and urban organization. It is not an urban-planning manual. Those mechanisms prevent V3 despite the explicitly unwanted urban/American center.
rationale: E/A credit historical research. S/U/M/F integrate infrastructure and institutions. Extensive local detail lowers D; R/N/P remain strong.

title: Civilisation
author: Kenneth Clark
reason: A narrative cultural history adapted from television scripts. It is a personal interpretive account, not an art-history workbook. Patronage, institutions and forms give modest payload; the narrow Western canon limits the implied universality.
rationale: E/M retain interpretive-selection limits; A credits art-historical expertise. S/U/F modest, D moderate. R/N/P credit durable visual narrative.

title: Clocks and Culture, 1300–1700
author: Carlo M. Cipolla
reason: A compact technological and economic history of clock production and diffusion. It is not instruction in clockmaking. Skills, demand, trade and cultural acceptance provide strong transferable mechanisms.
rationale: E/A credit historical scholarship. S/U/M/F integrate precision engineering and institutions. D/R/N/P credit concise durable explanation.

title: Coyote America
author: Dan Flores
reason: An explanatory natural and cultural history of coyotes. Adaptation, population response and policy feedback supply mechanisms. Ecology and American environmental history trigger T11; the inspected account is not primarily an environmental manifesto.
rationale: E/A credit scientific synthesis and observation. S/U/M concern adaptation and institutional response, F low. D/R/N/P retain readable durable history.

title: Democracy In America
author: Alexis de Tocqueville
reason: A comparative political and social argument based on American observation, not a civics textbook. Associations, equality, incentives and institutional checks provide durable payload. Normative reflections do not by themselves establish ideological capture or V5 activism.
rationale: E/M are limited by short observation and broad inference. S/U/F retain institutional mechanisms, A historical standing. D moderate; R/N/P strong.

title: Deng Xiaoping and The Transformation of China
author: Ezra F. Vogel
reason: A researched political biography explaining reform, incentives and institutional control. Industrial transformation supplies payload, but the central organizing subject remains a political leader. Access and elite-centered interpretation limit confidence.
rationale: E/A credit research with viewpoint limits. S/U/M/F connect institutions and economic reform. Length lowers D; R/N strong, P moderately restrained.

title: Diocletian and the Roman Recovery
author: Stephen Williams
reason: A general historical argument about Diocletian’s fiscal, military and administrative reforms. It offers institutional mechanisms and is not specialist technical instruction.
rationale: E/A credit historical scholarship with ancient-source limits. S/U/M/F concern state capacity. D/R/N/P credit focused durable narrative.

title: Dynasty
author: Tom Holland
reason: A narrative account of the Julio-Claudian rulers. Succession, elite incentives and concentrated authority give modest payload beyond personalities. Ancient hostile testimony limits psychological certainty.
rationale: E/A reflect source and interpretation limits. S/U/M/F concern political institutions. D moderate; R/N/P retain durable narrative.

title: Eisenhower
author: Stephen E. Ambrose
reason: The nominated Eisenhower biography is assessed from its original first-volume year 1983; later condensed or paperback editions do not reset age. Command, coalitions and executive decisions provide payload. Authorial reputation alone is not treated as proof of every reconstructed scene.
rationale: E/A credit research with access and reconstruction limits. S/U/M/F concern strategy and institutions. D low for scope; R/N/P remain moderate to strong.

title: English Culture and the Decline of the Industrial Spirit, 1850-1980
author: Martin J. Wiener
reason: A sustained historical argument linking cultural preferences to industrial performance. It addresses general informed readers rather than technical training. Cultural causation is hard to separate from structural economic causes; retain that uncertainty rather than assert a proven veto.
rationale: E/M/P are reduced for causal attribution. S/U/F connect institutions, culture and industry; A scholarly engagement. D/R strong, N moderately academic.

title: Eradication
author: Nancy Leys Stepan
reason: A historical explanation of disease-eradication campaigns, not medical guidance. Logistics, measurement, institutional goals and unintended effects provide transferable implementation lessons. Disease triggers T11 despite these merits.
rationale: E/A credit historical scholarship. S/U/M/F connect public institutions and operational constraints. D/R/N/P retain focused durable narrative.

title: The Fall of Constantinople 1453
author: Steven Runciman
reason: A narrative siege history with resources, fortification, diplomacy and coordination mechanisms. It is not a military manual; the cross-imperial case does not automatically trigger a single-nation deduction.
rationale: E/A credit historical scholarship with source-age limits. S/U/M/F concern operational constraints. D/R/N/P credit compact durable history.

title: Founding Brothers
author: Joseph J. Ellis
reason: Six historical episodes explain the fragility of early US institutions. Bargaining, precedent and coalition management offer transferable mechanisms. It is not civic instruction or a manifesto.
rationale: E/A credit scholarship; S/U/M/F concern political institutions. D/R/N/P credit focused durable coherent narrative.

title: History of the World
author: J. M. Roberts; Odd Arne Westad (revised edition)
reason: A general-reader continuous world history, not primarily a course textbook. It offers broad institutional connections but limited depth per case. The 2013 Roberts/Westad edition revises the work originally published in 1976, which remains the age basis.
rationale: E/A credit scholarly synthesis with compression limits. S/U/M/F broad but shallow. D low for immense length; R/N/P retain durable narrative.

title: How The Scots Invented The Modern World
author: Arthur Herman
reason: A general history of Scottish intellectual and institutional influence. Education and networks supply payload, but the national origin claim overstates exclusivity and causal scope. Low confidence is appropriate; the inspected evidence does not establish a serious veto.
rationale: E/M/P reduced for national attribution. S/U/F retain knowledge and institutional links. D/R/A/N moderate to strong.

title: Kelly: More Than My Share of It All
author: Clarence L. “Kelly” Johnson; Maggie Smith
reason: An aeronautical engineer’s memoir of aircraft development and project organization. It is not a design manual. Testing, autonomy and requirements provide direct payload, and the high-tech biography exception applies. Correct the later 1989 edition to 1985.
rationale: E/A credit firsthand practice with retrospective self-selection. S/U/M/F strongly connect engineering and organization. D/R/N/P credit focused durable account.

title: Life in the English Country House
author: Mark Girouard
reason: A cross-period social and architectural explanation of English country houses. Building forms, status and service organization provide payload. It is not an architectural practice reference; national history triggers T11.
rationale: E/A credit historical research. S/U/M/F connect material space and institutions. D/R/N/P credit durable clear visual explanation.

title: Lincoln at Gettysburg
author: Garry Wills
reason: A historical and rhetorical interpretation of the Gettysburg Address. Framing, legitimacy and the relation between words and institutions give modest payload, despite extremely low technical fit.
rationale: E/A credit scholarship; S/U/M/F modest institutional-rhetorical links. D/R/N/P credit compact durable argument.

title: Lost in Shangri-La
author: Mitchell Zuckoff
reason: A reported account of a crash and rescue. Logistics, communication and survival under constraints provide transferable payload. The central American wartime-disaster narrative triggers T11; combat doctrine is not central, so T12=0.
rationale: E/A credit reporting. S/U/M/F concern rescue operations. D/R/N/P retain focused durable readable narrative.

title: Memoirs or Chronicle of the Fourth Crusade and the Conquest of Constantinople
author: Geoffroi de Villehardouin
reason: A participant chronicle, not crusading instruction or a religious tract. Shipping contracts, debt, coalition breakdown and command constraints give payload. The author’s elite perspective and defense of his side constrain reliability. Use approximate composition 1210, within the reported 1207–1213 interval.
rationale: E/M/P are limited by partisan eyewitness testimony. A credits direct access; S/U/F concern campaign organization. D/R/N retain compact durable primary-source value.

title: Modern Times
author: Paul Johnson
reason: A general narrative interpretation of twentieth-century political history, not a course manual. Its strongly personalized moral interpretation and sweeping causal claims warrant low evidence and mechanism scores. A serious whole-book veto is not established merely from the author’s political reputation. The original 1983 work covers the 1920s–1980; later extensions do not reset publication age.
rationale: E/M/P are limited by selected causal interpretation. S/U/F retain broad institutional connections. D low for scope; R/N durable and readable, A general historian.

title: Mohammed and Charlemagne
author: Henri Pirenne
reason: A sustained historical explanation of trade, conquest and European institutions rather than technical training. The Pirenne thesis is a historically important but disputed account, not a settled modern description. First French publication was 1937; 1939 is the English translation.
rationale: E/M/P reduced for an expansive contested causal thesis. S/U/F integrate trade and state formation, A scholarly influence. D/R strong, N moderately academic.

title: Moorish Spain
author: Richard Fletcher
reason: A compact general history of Islamic Iberia, not religious advocacy or a specialist manual. Conquest, exchange, fragmentation and institutional coexistence supply payload. Correct the catalog’s reprint year to 1992.
rationale: E/A credit historical scholarship; S/U/M/F connect institutions and cultural exchange. D/R/N/P credit concise durable explanation.

title: Mortal Republic
author: Edward J. Watts
reason: A general historical explanation of the Roman Republic’s institutional failure. Rules, compromise, violence and incentives provide transferable mechanisms; contemporary parallels do not alone make it activism. Use the transition to the Augustan settlement in 27 BCE as the central endpoint, with the 22 BCE opening scene as aftermath.
rationale: E/A credit classical scholarship with ancient-source limits. S/U/M/F concern institutional failure. D/R/N/P retain focused durable narrative.

title: No Applause - Just Throw Money
author: Trav S.D.
reason: A history of the American vaudeville business. Touring circuits, audience selection and changing entertainment technology provide modest transferable payload. Its media and American entertainment center triggers both themes. The central vaudeville era is assessed as ending around 1930, despite discussion of its later legacy.
rationale: E/A credit researched theatrical history. S/U/M explain entertainment markets, F very low. D moderate; R/N/P retain historical and narrative value.

title: Ordinary Men
author: Christopher R. Browning
reason: A historical investigation of Reserve Police Battalion 101, not police instruction. Testimony, command, conformity and situational incentives provide transferable institutional mechanisms. Retrospective perpetrator testimony limits causal certainty; the account does not require racial or political allegiance.
rationale: E/A credit archival investigation with testimony limits. S/U/M/F concern obedience and institutional violence. D/R/N/P credit focused durable argument.

title: Origin Story
author: David Christian
reason: A continuous explanatory history from cosmology to human societies, not a Big History course workbook. Energy flows and thresholds provide integration, but breadth limits causal detail and much basic physics has low incremental value for this reader.
rationale: E/A credit scholarly synthesis with compression limits. S high, U/M/F moderate for a physicist. D moderate; R/N/P retain readable broad explanation.

title: Pandaemonium 1660–1886
author: Humphrey Jennings
reason: A curated documentary account of industrial transformation through contemporary voices. Literary excerpts are components of a nonfiction historical anthology, not grounds to classify the whole book as a novel. Juxtaposition exposes experience and production changes but supplies less explicit causal analysis.
rationale: E/A credit primary testimony while separating observation from literary representation. S/U/F link technology and society; M modest. D/R strong, N/P depend on fragmentary form.

title: Red Star Over The Pacific
author: Toshi Yoshihara; James R. Holmes
reason: An explanatory strategic argument about Chinese sea power and American responses, not a naval operations manual. Geography, fleet capabilities and strategic incentives give payload. Assess the original argument historically; the 2010 force inventory is not current intelligence.
rationale: E/A credit language access and naval expertise. S/U/M/F connect capabilities and geography. D strong, R limited by changing forces; N/P analytical.

title: River Out of Eden
author: Richard Dawkins
reason: A compact public explanation of genetic information and selection, not biology training. Gene-centered reasoning supplies mechanisms. Criticism of teleology does not turn this work into a religious book; accessible science retains value but direct fit is limited.
rationale: E/A credit scientific authority; M/U explain selection, S/F moderate. D/R/N/P credit concise durable and precise exposition.

title: Rubicon
author: Tom Holland
reason: Narrative history of the Republic’s transformation into imperial rule. Elite competition, military loyalty and institutional breakdown provide payload. Ancient testimony and dramatic reconstruction limit certainty.
rationale: E/A credit researched synthesis with source limits. S/U/M/F concern institutional competition. D moderate; R/N/P retain durable cumulative history.

title: Son of the Morning Star
author: Evan S. Connell
reason: A literary historical account of Custer, the Plains wars and Little Bighorn. Command failure, information and conflicting incentives provide modest payload beyond biography. Racial and American military history trigger both deductions.
rationale: E/A credit historical inquiry with reconstruction limits. S/U/M/F modest command interpretation. D low for digressions; R/N/P credit durable narrative.

title: Spain in Our Hearts
author: Adam Hochschild
reason: A history of Americans in the Spanish Civil War, not a campaign manual or an activist program. Oil supply, credit, propaganda and international nonintervention give mechanisms beyond individual volunteers.
rationale: E/A credit archival reporting. S/U/M/F connect supply and political constraints. D moderate; R/N/P retain durable clear narrative.

title: The American Story
author: David M. Rubenstein
reason: Interviews with historians about American history. Historical interpretation and institutional comparisons supply modest payload; the question-and-answer format is not technical training. It remains a broad, personality-heavy introduction.
rationale: E/A depend on interviewees rather than new independent research. S/U/M/F limited by separate conversations. D/R/N/P retain accessible durable interpretation.

title: The Battle of Alcazar
author: E.W. Bovill
reason: A narrative account of the 1578 Moroccan battle and its Iberian consequences. Coalition, logistics and dynastic risk provide some transfer. It is a cross-regional campaign case, not a military textbook.
rationale: E/A credit historical research with dated-source limits. S/U/M/F concern military-political constraints. D/R strong, N/P moderately scholarly.

title: The City In History
author: Lewis Mumford
reason: A sustained comparative history of cities rather than a planning manual. Infrastructure, social organization and technology provide integration. Normative judgments and broad historical generalization reduce precision; the urban center triggers T11.
rationale: E/M/P reflect expansive interpretation. S/U/F connect built form and institutions, A specialist standing. D low for length, R high, N moderately academic.

title: The Craft
author: John Dickie
reason: A researched international history of Freemasonry, not a craft manual or a conspiracy tract. Networks, trust, secrecy and changing relations with states provide mechanisms. Religious and conspiratorial beliefs are objects of historical analysis.
rationale: E/A credit historical scholarship; S/U/M/F concern networks and institutional power. D moderate for wide scope; R/N/P retain durable clear history.

title: The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
author: Edward Gibbon
reason: A general historical synthesis of the Roman and Byzantine empires, not a technical reference. Institutions, revenue, military organization and religious authority provide payload. Treat its Enlightenment interpretation and obsolete scholarship historically, not as a current consensus. First volume 1776 governs series age.
rationale: E/M reflect old source base and broad attribution. S/U/F integrate institutions, A enduring historiographical standing. D low for six-volume length; R/N/P credit lasting literary architecture.

title: The Discovery of France
author: Graham Robb
reason: A historical explanation of how local languages, routes and communities became a more integrated France. Mapping, transport and standardization provide transferable mechanisms. National cultural history remains central.
rationale: E/A credit archival and geographical research. S/U/M/F connect information and integration. D moderate for local detail; R/N/P strong.

title: The Fifteen Decisive Battles of the World
author: Edward Creasy
reason: A narrative selection of battles, not tactical training. Geography, organization and decisions give some transfer. The author explicitly rejects fatalism, but the decisive-battle selection still depends on hard-to-test counterfactual attribution and an old source base.
rationale: E/M/P reduced for selection and counterfactual inference. S/U/F retain campaign constraints. D/A/N moderate to low, R high as historical interpretation.

title: The First Conspiracy
author: Brad Meltzer; Josh Mensch
reason: A popular historical account of a plot against Washington. Security, incentives and fragile institutions supply modest payload, but thriller reconstruction limits confidence in scene-level claims.
rationale: E/A/P reflect narrative-reconstruction limits. S/U/M/F modest institutional and security explanation. D/R/N credit an accessible bounded account.

title: The Fortunes of Africa
author: Martin Meredith
reason: A continent-wide history of resource extraction, trade and political control. It is not a single-nation history or chiefly a civil-rights narrative. Commercial routes, commodities and state incentives provide integration; political control is central enough for T12.
rationale: E/A credit researched synthesis with compression limits. S/U/M/F connect resources, trade and power. D low for large scope; R/N/P retain durable narrative.

title: The Future Is Asian
author: Parag Khanna
reason: A broad account of Asian economic networks combined with a strong forecast. Infrastructure and trade supply a durable payload, so prediction does not alone establish V4. Uncertain aggregation and the confident Asian-century frame sharply limit evidence and durability.

author: Gregory Zuckerman

title: The Tycoons
author: Charles R. Morris

author: Ronald W. Chan

author: Ben Macintyre

author: Oliver Stone

author: Mark Owen; Kevin Maurer

Differing accounts and limited independent access reduce confidence rather than establish a specific serious veto here.

title: No Ordinary Time
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
